body.statement: For every admissible radius triple \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), the rule \(\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}\) from def:clipped-score and def:oracle-threshold belongs to \(\mathcal T_n\). There is a constant \(C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants, including \(M\) and \(M_Y\), such that \(\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}E_P|\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}-\tau(P)|\le C\rho_n\). The same estimator satisfies \(\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}-\tau(P)|>C\rho_n/\delta\}\le\delta\) for every fixed \(\delta\in(0,1/4)\).
body.justification: It supplies one feasible procedure attaining all four components without strengthening global \(L^2(P_X)\) information.
body.gap: Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics proves a sufficient studentized limit, and MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, gives asymptotic inference for a bias-corrected trimmed ATE estimator that preserves the original target; neither establishes the finite-risk public-function upper frontier obtained from the \(r_{1n}/\sqrt{n\lambda}\) stochastic term.
body.consumer: Analysts with certified black-box prediction errors obtain a clipping rule for the original population ATE rather than a trimmed-population estimand.
